articles.title: Noboa's China visit to deepen Ecuador-China ties
articles.titleCn: 诺沃亚访华将深化厄中关系
articles.summary: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa is set to make his first state visit to China this month, a trip that comes as the two countries mark a decade of their comprehensive strategic partnership and seek to turn growing trade ties into broader cooperation.
articles.summaryCn: 厄瓜多尔总统诺沃亚首次国事访问中国，旨在深化两国全面战略伙伴关系，并推动贸易增长向更广泛合作扩展。

paragraphs.en:
a is set to make his first state visit to China this month, a trip that comes as the two countries mark a decade of their {{1}} {{2}} partnership and seek to turn growing trade ties into broader cooperation. For Noboa, the visit will be another step in a relationship that has become increasingly important to Ecuador's economic strategy. The 38-year-old former businessman has stressed that Ecuador should maintain commercial ties with a range of major economies. Growing trade ties
Ecuador's exports grew 6.4% in 2025, according to its central bank, with shrimp, cocoa, bananas and mining products among the main {{15}} of exports, while China has become a major destination for those products and a key source of imports. The trade relationship between the two countries has gained even stronger {{3}} since the China-Ecuador free trade agreement took effect in May 2024.
paragraphs.cn: 诺沃亚将于本月对中国进行首次国事访问，此行正值两国庆祝全面战略伙伴关系十周年，并寻求将日益增长的贸易关系转化为更广泛的合作。对诺沃亚而言，此次访问将是这段对厄瓜多尔经济战略日益重要的关系中的又一步。这位38岁的前商人强调，厄瓜多尔应与多个主要经济体保持商业联系。厄瓜多尔央行数据显示，2025年该国出口增长6.4%，虾、可可、香蕉和矿产品是主要出口驱动力，而中国已成为这些产品的主要目的地和重要进口来源。自2024年5月中厄自由贸易协定生效以来，两国贸易关系势头更加强劲。

In 2025, bilateral trade reached $17.33 billion, up 24% year-on-year, with Ecuador's exports to China rising 19.3% to $9.55 billion, {{17}} a trade {{4}} of $1.77 billion for Ecuador. The upward trend continued into 2026, with bilateral trade reaching $4.756 billion in the first quarter, up 21.42% from a year earlier, while Ecuador's exports to China rose 13.8% to $2.663 billion. The agreement is gradually lowering {{5}} and improving market access, creating room for Ecuador to expand sales of agricultural and other products while giving Chinese companies greater access to the Ecuadorian market. In an interview with Ecuadorian media last month, Gao Zhenting, China's consul general in Guayaquil, the largest city in Ecuador, said China and Ecuador have highly {{6}} economies, with trade and economic cooperation serving as a key foundation of bilateral ties and delivering {{7}} benefits to both peoples.

paragraphs.cn: 诺沃亚本人与中国的接触也在加速。2025年6月在北京期间，他见证了推动“一带一路”倡议合作计划的签署。诺沃亚表示，厄瓜多尔期待深化与中国的关系，并加强在贸易、科技、文化、教育和青年领域的合作。此次访问的时机值得注意。中国与厄瓜多尔正庆祝建交46周年及全面战略伙伴关系十周年，近期的交流也凸显了对扩大合作的支持。

paragraphs.cn: 中国官员表示，愿巩固政治互信，深化各领域合作，而厄瓜多尔议员则对加强与中国的关系表达了广泛支持。

articles.fullText:
a is set to make his first state visit to China this month, a trip that comes as the two countries mark a decade of their comprehensive strategic partnership and seek to turn growing trade ties into broader cooperation.
For Noboa, the visit will be another step in a relationship that has become increasingly important to Ecuador's economic strategy. The 38-year-old former businessman has stressed that Ecuador should maintain commercial ties with a range of major economies.
Growing trade ties
Ecuador's exports grew 6.4% in 2025, according to its central bank, with shrimp, cocoa, bananas and mining products among the main drivers of exports, while China has become a major destination for those products and a key source of imports.
The trade relationship between the two countries has gained even stronger momentum since the China-Ecuador free trade agreement took effect in May 2024. According to China's official data, Ecuador's exports to China jumped 10.1% in the first eight months after the agreement entered into force, far outpacing its overall annual growth.
In 2025, bilateral trade reached $17.33 billion, up 24% year-on-year, with Ecuador's exports to China rising 19.3% to $9.55 billion, generating a trade surplus of $1.77 billion for Ecuador. The upward trend continued into 2026, with bilateral trade reaching $4.756 billion in the first quarter, up 21.42% from a year earlier, while Ecuador's exports to China rose 13.8% to $2.663 billion.
The agreement is gradually lowering tariffs and improving market access, creating room for Ecuador to expand sales of agricultural and other products while giving Chinese companies greater access to the Ecuadorian market. In an interview with Ecuadorian media last month, Gao Zhenting, China's consul general in Guayaquil, the largest city in Ecuador, said China and Ecuador have highly complementary economies, with trade and economic cooperation serving as a key foundation of bilateral ties and delivering tangible benefits to both peoples.
He emphasized that China supports trade and investment liberalization and seeks to expand the global economic "pie" rather than pursue trade surpluses, highlighting China's vast consumer market and investment potential as opportunities for Ecuador.
Broader cooperation
The broader bilateral relationship provides a foundation for the growing economic integration. China and Ecuador established diplomatic ties in 1980, formed a strategic partnership in 2015 and upgraded it to a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2016. Ecuador and China signed a Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) memorandum of understanding in 2018.
Cooperation has extended into energy, mining, electricity and infrastructure, while the two governments have continued to identify clean energy, infrastructure and finance as areas for further collaboration.
Noboa's own engagement with China has also accelerated. During his stay in Beijing in June 2025, he witnessed the signing of a cooperation plan on promoting the BRI. Noboa said Ecuador looked forward to deepening relations with China and increasing cooperation in trade, science and technology, culture, education and youth.
The timing of the new visit is notable. China and Ecuador are marking 46 years of diplomatic relations and the 10th anniversary of their comprehensive strategic partnership, while recent exchanges have underscored support for expanding cooperation. Chinese officials have said they are ready to consolidate political mutual trust and deepen cooperation across fields, while Ecuadorian lawmakers have voiced broad support for stronger ties with China.

articles.title: English hospitals aim to ramp up use of robotics in surgery
articles.titleCn: 英国医院旨在加大机器人手术应用力度
articles.summary: The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035
articles.summaryCn: 英国政府计划投资机器人设备，目标到2035年90%的微创手术使用机器人辅助，以提升手术精准度并缓解医疗系统压力。

paragraphs.en:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in {{1}} equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of {{2}} surgeries carried out in England by 2035. The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other {{3}} technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables. Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an {{4}} 3D headset and a video-game-like {{5}}.
paragraphs.cn: 英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。外科医生和护士在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

paragraphs.en:
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of {{6}} including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery. Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The {{7}} of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker {{8}} times, which will take {{9}} off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge {{10}}. "The ability to have lots of {{11}} computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
paragraphs.cn: 在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受培训使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统的人员。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头戴设备和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

paragraphs.en:
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of {{12}} like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery. Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to {{13}} lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this {{14}} title, but the news "didn't {{15}}" the 76-year-old retired detective. Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet.
paragraphs.cn: 此类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右），高级心胸外科培训生，正在机器人专科培训中观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

paragraphs.en: "It was {{16}}," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." "They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."

articles.fullText:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."
articles.fullTextCn:
英国政府宣布计划增加对英格兰医院机器人设备的投资，并设定目标，到2035年，英格兰90%的微创手术将使用机器人辅助。政府将机器人技术列为英格兰十年健康计划中的五大“重大赌注”之一，其他变革性技术包括数据、人工智能、基因组学和可穿戴设备。外科医生和护士在伦敦圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

在伦敦市中心的圣巴塞洛缪医院，来访的外科医生是首批接受培训使用美国公司Initiative制造的新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统的人员。该系统包括三个可持手术器械的机械臂，通过沉浸式3D头戴设备和类似视频游戏的控制台进行操作。

此类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右），高级心胸外科培训生，正在机器人专科培训中观摩。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间和加快恢复速度，这将减轻一个面临漫长等待名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈的医疗系统的压力。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准、安全，”巴特健康NHS信托机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善恢复时间，更高的精准度还降低了并发症风险，如空气泄漏，这是肺手术后住院时间延长的常见原因。护士在圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新的达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统协助肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中第一位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到他穿上手术服并被麻醉，他才意识到自己将获得这一开创性称号，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后三十分钟，Macleod就重新站了起来。

“这太不可思议了，”他说。“事实上，手术后我很快发现我只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示恢复时间“长得多”。这次，不到一周后，他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院开展专科培训，教授外科医生这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能，”他说，“他们可能带来了游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”

在阐述他的长期使命时，Stamenkovic补充道：“我们只需要利用他们的精力、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”

articles.fullText:
Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries.
A scorched landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. 
France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France.
Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record.
Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people.
Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026. 
In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF.
A forest fire is also raging in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, comparable to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018.
The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Neighboring Hungary has extended its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as forecasts show the heat wave will continue. Authorities warned that persistent high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take precautions.
The heat wave has intensified drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day.
A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. 
Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 monitored cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo.
Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop yields and higher irrigation demand.
A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained operational but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance.
Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational disruptions as high river temperatures affected cooling capacity.
The combination of extreme heat, drought and declining water availability is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.

articles.fullText:
Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz slowed over the weekend, data showed on Monday, following attacks on tankers, as talks between the US and Iran stalled.
Five commodity vessels transited the strait on Saturday, with none registered for Sunday, shiptracking data from Kpler showed. The prior weekend recorded 31 vessels.
Ships entering the strait on Saturday included an empty Very Large Crude Carrier with its Automatic Identification System switched off and an Indian-flagged Very Large Gas Carrier that used the Iranian route, Kpler data showed.
A small tanker carrying Iranian fuel oil exited, it showed.
Shipping appeared to grind to a near standstill after the United Arab Emirates said three vessels operated by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company were attacked in transit last week.
The United States said it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely.
Some ships may pass through undetected with transponders off, but the figures are far from the more than 130 ships a day that traversed the Strait of Hormuz before the war launched by the US and Israel on Iran in February.
Washington must meet Iran's conditions regarding the strait in order for shipping to resume, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with local media on Saturday.
The waterway handled a fifth of the world's shipments of crude oil and liquefied natural gas before the war.
At the Bab el-Mandeb strait, where Yemeni Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia on July 20, Kpler data showed 49 weekend transits by commodity vessels, down from 55 in the prior week. There were no tracked Saudi oil shipments.
Iran says US forces expelled
Chief Commander of the Iranian Army Amir Hatami said on Sunday that US forces have been expelled from the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and the Strait of Hormuz, and are prohibited from returning.
Hatami said US military bases in the region could by no means return to their previous state, and Iran will never allow such a situation to happen.
He also rebuked the US president for his recent remarks, saying Trump's backtracking after declaring the Strait of Hormuz part of American territory demonstrated his failure to come to terms with reality and his determination to project an image of victory despite setbacks.
Hatami's remarks came after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US military has the capability to maintain a naval presence in the region to enforce its retaliatory blockade of Iran.
"Indefinitely the United States Navy can maintain a blockade like that because we'll rotate ships in and out, as we have, and we'll continue to," Hegseth told reporters during a trip to Panama.

在曼德海峡，也门胡塞武装于7月20日宣布对沙特阿拉伯实施海上封锁，Kpler数据显示周末有49艘商品船通过，低于前一周的55艘。没有追踪到沙特的石油运输。伊朗表示美军已被驱逐。伊朗陆军总司令阿米尔·哈塔米周日表示，美军已被驱逐出波斯湾、阿曼湾和霍尔木兹海峡，并被禁止返回。哈塔米表示，美国在该地区的军事基地绝不可能恢复到以前的状态，伊朗绝不允许这种情况发生。他还斥责了美国总统最近的言论，称特朗普在宣布霍尔木兹海峡为美国领土后出尔反尔，表明他未能面对现实，并决心在遭遇挫折的情况下塑造胜利形象。

哈塔米的言论是在美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯表示美军有能力在该地区保持海军存在以执行对伊朗的报复性封锁之后发表的。赫格塞斯在访问巴拿马期间对记者说：“美国海军可以无限期维持这样的封锁，因为我们会像现在这样轮换船只进出，而且我们会继续这样做。”

articles.fullText:
Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a reshuffling at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure.
Hassabis will take on two new titles, Alphabet announced on Wednesday: chair of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet.
The change "will allow me to focus on long-term strategy, and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning into my work at Isomorphic to help cure disease," Hassabis wrote in a social media post.
Isomorphic Labs is an AI-powered drug discovery lab that spun out from DeepMind in 2021. In 2024, Hassabis won a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
As part of the shake up, DeepMind's chief technology officer and chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu will become the division's senior vice president and oversee its operations, including the development of Google's flagship frontier models and products which are known as Gemini.
Longtime Google engineer Jeff Dean is also leaving the company after nearly three decades to "try something new, and we're excited to support him in that," Google CEO Sundar Pichai said in a blog post announcing the news.
Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in 2010, and four years later, Google bought the research lab for $650 million, according to reports at the time. His co-founder, Mustafa Suleyman, is currently the chief of Microsoft's AI segment.
Google is competing for customers alongside other major AI developers including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as well as DeepSeek and Moonshot in China.
The industry is also chasing a theoretical milestone known as advanced general intelligence (AGI), which is a point when AI software matches the capabilities of human thinking.
"I've been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand," Hassabis wrote in Wednesday's blog post.
"With this backdrop, I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at (Google DeepMind), so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come," Hassabis continued.
Observers have been waiting for Google to announce a more powerful version of its AI model, called Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was supposed to launch in June but appears to be delayed.
Its shares closed 4% down Wednesday afternoon.
The leadership changes come amid a wider brain drain at Google.
In June, a top AI and engineering executive, Noam Shazeer, left for OpenAI, while senior researcher John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Hassabis, jumped to Anthropic.

谷歌AI负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯将卸任当前职务，成为Alphabet的首席科学家，与此同时DeepMind进行重组，包括一名关键工程师的离职。Alphabet于周三宣布，哈萨比斯将担任两个新职务：DeepMind主席和Alphabet首席科学家。哈萨比斯在社交媒体帖子中写道，这一变动“将使我能够专注于长期战略，并加速科学突破，包括深入我在Isomorphic的工作以帮助治愈疾病。”Isomorphic Labs是一家AI驱动的药物发现实验室，于2021年从DeepMind分拆出来。2024年，哈萨比斯获得了诺贝尔化学奖。

作为重组的一部分，DeepMind的首席技术官兼首席AI架构师Koray Kavukcuoglu将成为该部门的高级副总裁，并负责其运营，包括开发谷歌旗舰前沿模型和产品，即Gemini。谷歌长期工程师Jeff Dean在近三十年后也将离开公司，以“尝试新事物，我们很高兴支持他这样做，”谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在宣布此消息的博客文章中表示。哈萨比斯于2010年共同创立了DeepMind，四年后，据当时报道，谷歌以6.5亿美元收购了该研究实验室。他的联合创始人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼目前是微软AI部门的主管。谷歌正在与其他主要AI开发者竞争客户，包括微软、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，以及中国的DeepSeek和Moonshot。

该行业还在追逐一个理论里程碑，即高级通用智能（AGI），这是AI软件达到人类思维能力水平的时刻。“我一生都在致力于AGI，现在，像你们许多人一样，我觉得它近在咫尺，”哈萨比斯在周三的博客文章中写道。“在这种背景下，我决定现在是时候将我在（谷歌DeepMind）的日常运营职责移交出去，以便我有时间和空间专注于大局，并帮助影响未来，”哈萨比斯继续说道。观察者一直在等待谷歌宣布其更强大的AI模型版本，称为Gemini 3.5 Pro，该模型原定于6月推出，但似乎被推迟了。其股价周三下午收盘下跌4%。

领导层变动发生在谷歌更广泛的人才流失背景下。6月，顶级AI和工程高管Noam Shazeer离开去了OpenAI，而高级研究员John Jumper（与哈萨比斯共同获得2024年诺贝尔化学奖）跳槽到了Anthropic。
